reader.notes: ScreenControlItemsDistinct compares the resolved items (ReferenceEquals) at 85 only, so a repeat in any spelling or position is refused and distinct items pass; 2002+ use the written-reference check instead, as their own text says. A level-66 rename of an operand is accepted as a different data item (its own entry, §1985:VI.5.11); the 1985 text does not settle whether a rename identifies 'a different data item', so this is the one reading-dependent edge.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: cfinal (CONTROLS ARE FINAL B A B OF G) COBOL1699, so FINAL and an intervening operand do not hide the repeat; ctwo (RD RPT CONTROLS B C with C REDEFINES G, plus a second RD CONTROL IS B) compiles and runs, so the screen is per report and overlapping-but-different items pass. Read ReportSectionBinder.cs#ScreenControlItemsDistinct: ReferenceEquals on the resolved items, below 2002 only. cite.py --check "§1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR2" "Each recurrence of data-name-1 must identify a different data item" -> OK. The reader's c08 (CONTROLS ARE B R66, R66 RENAMES B) compiles. The 1985 glossary defines Data Item as 'A unit of data (excluding literals) defined by a COBOL program' and RENAMES as 'alternative, possibly overlapping, groupings of elementary items' (§1985:VI.5.11): under the reading that 66 R66 RENAMES B names the same unit of data as B, the two recurrences identify one data item and c08 must be refused (under-rejects); under the reader's reading (a separate entry is a different data item) it conforms. The text does not decide it.
